name: UUID Generator
description: Generate UUID v1, v4 and v7 in batches, with configurable formatting.

hints.version: v4 is random, v1 is time based, and v7 sorts by time, which makes it a good primary key.
hints.format: Turning off "Keep hyphens" strips the separators, and "Wrap in braces" adds `{'{}'}`.
hints.output: The result can be copied in one click; a batch prints one UUID per line.

faq.a: Use v4 for random identifiers, v7 for primary keys that should keep insertion order, and v1 when an existing system expects the older time based form.

faq.q: Why is v7 a better primary key?
faq.a: A v7 starts with a millisecond timestamp, so lexicographic order roughly matches creation order, which keeps index writes friendly.
The random bits come from a cryptographically secure source; v1 and v7 additionally use a monotonic clock, so they do not repeat within the same millisecond.
